correctness.rationale: In each heavy chart the nontrivial ages are explicitly \((rk+(kb\bmod a))/a\) and \((rk+(ka\bmod b))/b\). Within the canonical triangle \(d=b-a\le r\), \(a\le r+d\), the displayed inequalities show every \(k\ge2\) age is at least the \(k=1\) age, giving the closed minimum formula. On the canonical boundary one first age equals one, while strict terminal inequalities make both chart minima greater than one. For terminal \(d>0\), \(B_1=1+(r-d)/b\), with \(d\le r-1\) and \(b\le r+2d-1\le3r-3\); equality forces \(d=r-1\), \(a=2r-2\), \(b=3r-3\), and the other chart is strictly higher. The inspected exact verifier exhausts all group elements through \(r=60\) as a regression check; the infinite theorem is established by the symbolic inequalities.
risks: The invariant is explicitly the minimum of the two heavy-chart Reid–Tai ages; no broader global minimal-log-discrepancy normalization is asserted.
